question: Which of the following correctly pairs the pathophysiological phase of allergic rhinitis with its predominant clinical manifestation?

answers.text: Early phase (0–30 min): nasal congestion and hyposmia; driven by newly synthesised leukotrienes from mast cells.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The early phase is dominated by preformed mediators (histamine, tryptase) causing sneezing, itching, and watery rhinorrhoea. Nasal congestion is predominantly a late-phase phenomenon driven by inflammatory cell infiltration (eosinophils, basophils).

answers.text: Early phase (0–30 min): sneezing, itching, watery rhinorrhoea; driven by histamine released from degranulating mast cells.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Antigen cross-linking of IgE on sensitised mast cells triggers immediate degranulation releasing histamine, prostaglandins, and tryptase — causing the classic early-phase triad of sneezing, pruritus, and profuse watery rhinorrhoea within minutes of allergen exposure.

answers.text: Late phase (4–8 h): sneezing and itching; driven by IgE cross-linking on re-exposure.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sneezing and itching are early-phase symptoms caused by histamine. The late phase (4–8 hours) is characterised by nasal congestion, hyposmia, and thick discharge as eosinophils and basophils infiltrate the mucosa — driven by newly synthesised cytokines and chemokines, not re-exposure IgE cross-linking.

answers.text: Both phases produce identical symptoms; the difference is only in their timing relative to allergen exposure.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The two phases have distinct symptom profiles. Early phase = sneezing, itching, watery discharge (histamine-mediated). Late phase = congestion, hyposmia, thick discharge (eosinophil/cytokine-mediated). This distinction is clinically important for choosing the right drug class.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the pathophysiology section carefully. The two-phase model directly informs drug selection: antihistamines for early phase; steroids for late phase.
Correct. Early phase = histamine = sneezing and watery rhinorrhoea. Late phase = eosinophilic inflammation = congestion and hyposmia.
